title: processkit-cli `list --json` registry entry
description: One line of `processkit-cli list --json`: the command prints one JSON object per registry entry, one per line (JSON Lines), ordered deterministically by `run_id` then `started_at`. An empty registry prints no lines at all and exits 0. This is the client's own display shape, deliberately decoupled from the on-disk registry record (docs/registry.md, "Record format") — it never carries the record's lock file name or `registry_version`. The normative prose is docs/registry.md, "Discovery — `list`"; the in-code source of truth is src/list.rs. Validated against fixtures/schema/cli/list.jsonl, and against the real binary's output, by tests/machine_output.rs.

rfc3339Millis.description: RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision (`…Z`) — the same formatter every other timestamp in this binary uses.

listEntry.description: One registered run as `list --json` prints it.

run_id.description: The run's identifier — the value a caller passes as `--run-id` to `inspect`/`cancel`/`kill`/`wait`. Not unique: the registry does not enforce uniqueness (docs/registry.md, "Run id resolution").

health.description: `live` — a runner still holds the entry's liveness lock; `stale` — a **confirmed** leftover from a runner that died without cleaning up; `unprobed` — the liveness lock could not even be opened (permission denied, a rejected symlink/reparse point, a non-regular file in its place), so liveness is genuinely unknown and is never reported as the confirmed-dead `stale`. All three are listed, never hidden.

hint.description: The run's worker-shape category (`msbuild_node_reuse`, …) from the same classifier catalog the JSONL `run_started` event uses (docs/schema.md, "Hint classifier"), or null for the common case of a command matching no known shape — and for a record written before the field existed. A fixed category label, never command-line content; the catalog grows additively and docs/schema.md is its single source of truth.

argv_sha256.description: The run's one-way argv fingerprint — lowercase-hex SHA-256, in full (the human-readable table abbreviates it instead), so a caller can join this entry to the `argv_sha256` of the same run's `run_started` event byte for byte. Null for a record written before the field existed, or one whose value did not survive the registry's read-side shape guard.

labels.description: Operator labels in full, empty when the run carried none. Keys and values are re-validated when the record is read back (src/labels.rs); a value that fails validation is dropped from the map rather than failing the whole record.

jsonl.description: Absolute path to the run's JSONL lifecycle stream, or null when the record publishes none.

capture_dir.description: Absolute output-capture directory, or null when the run was started without `--capture-dir`.

endpoint.description: The run's local control-transport address (a unix socket path or a Windows named pipe name), or null when the transport was never stood up — best-effort degradation, and never populated again for a stale entry's original runner, though the last-published value stays whatever the record said.
